### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A: one parsing rule and one lifetime rule for the five numerics switches `SNAP_WB_REF4`,
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, `SNAP_FLUX_COVARIANCE`, `SNAP_X1_MASS_COVARIANCE` and
`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`.

**Data.** In: the environment string of each variable at the first call of its accessor. Out: one cached
boolean per accessor, shared by every block of the process.

**Placement.** The first call of an accessor, which can happen during setup before any time step; the value
is then fixed for the life of the process.

**Activation.** Three switches default to off (WB, XC, MC); two default to on: FC, whose lookup falls back to
`"1"` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}), and RE, whose lookup falls back to `"1"`
as well ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::gravity_work_radial_exact >}}). XC turns WB on.

**Guarantee / limits.** The parse is a lower-cased comparison with four false tokens; no trimming, no
validation of spelling, and nothing checks that the ranks of a run agree.

**Evidence.** `test_horizontal_flux_covariance_python` and `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` each compare
the unset arm with the `1` arm bit for bit and the `0` arm against it
({{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py main >}},
{{< code tests/test_gravity_work_radial_exact.py main >}}); check `[C1]` of `configuration_check.py`; the
ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

The five numerics switches are study flags: they change the scheme for the whole run and every block must make
the same choice, or the shared faces of the mesh stop being single-valued. The code reads each of them once per
process and never again, which is why this section exists apart from the switches themselves: an A/B comparison
of a switch needs one child process per arm, and a flag set between two stages of one process does nothing.

| value, compared after lower-casing | WB, XC, MC | FC | RE |
|---|---|---|---|
| unset | off | on | on |
| empty string | off | off | on |
| `0`, `false`, `off`, `no` | off | off | off |
| every other string | on | on | on |

: The parse of the five numerics switches at the pin. {#tbl-ch12-environment-parse}

There is no trimming: `false ` with a trailing space is "every other string" and turns a switch on. Every block
in one process sees the same cached value; the code does not by itself make different MPI processes agree.

### Derivation

No numerical equation is added. `get_env` ({{< code src/layout/layout.hpp get_env >}}) returns the environment
string when the variable is set, otherwise the default the caller passes. Each accessor lower-cases the string,
compares it with `0`, `false`, `off` and `no`, and stores the result in a function-local static. The three
off-by-default accessors and `HydroImpl::flux_covariance` also count the empty string as off;
`HydroImpl::gravity_work_radial_exact` does not, so an empty value leaves it on. Check line `[C1]` enumerates
this truth table over nine values for both rules and the implication from XC to WB with and without gravity
[check `src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

Launch child A with its environment, let its first accessor call fix the flag, then run all its blocks with
that cached value; launch child B separately for the other arm. The first call can occur during setup, before
a time step, so changing a flag between RK stages is not a valid experiment, and a test that inherits the
user's environment can run a nominal default arm with a switch set by the shell.

#| fig-cap: "Environment parsing and process lifetime: labelled boxes show inputs and decisions in evaluation order. This is a configuration or stencil diagram, not measured data."
#| fig-alt: "parent sets environment; child A first read; cached A for all blocks; child B: fresh read."
#| echo: false

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| re arms | {{< code tests/test_gravity_work_radial_exact.py ARMS >}} | `ARMS` | `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` |

: Implementation sites for the environment switches. {#tbl-ch12-environment-code}

1. Read the string, or the accessor's default when the variable is absent. The anchor `get_env` is in
   {{< code src/layout/layout.hpp get_env >}}.
2. Lower-case it, compare with the false tokens (the empty string included for all but RE), and cache the
   boolean. The anchor `flux_covariance` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}; the
   anchor `gravity_work_radial_exact` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::gravity_work_radial_exact >}}.
3. Let XC imply WB: `wb_ref4_enabled` returns true when `x1_centroid_exact_enabled` does. The anchor
   `wb_ref4_enabled` is in {{< code src/hydro/wb_ref4.cpp wb_ref4_enabled >}}.

| `test_gravity_work_radial_exact_python` | the unset arm equals the `1` arm bit for bit; the `0` arm differs | `torch.equal` | the script |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-environment-tests}

The arm dictionaries are `ARMS` in {{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py ARMS >}} and
{{< code tests/test_gravity_work_radial_exact.py ARMS >}}; the comparisons are in each script's `main`
({{< code tests/test_horizontal_flux_covariance.py main >}},
{{< code tests/test_gravity_work_radial_exact.py main >}}).

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch15-ch12-tests.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The independent parser check models the documented contract; it does not execute the C++ static storage.
Cross-rank consistency is a launch responsibility. Any string outside the four false tokens (and the empty
string where it counts) silently turns a switch on.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
